correctness.rationale: The mathematical deductions are correct. A topology on a finite set has only finitely many distinct opens, so every arbitrary intersection of opens is a finite intersection and the topology is Alexandrov. For an Alexandrov space its opens are exactly the up-sets of the specialization preorder, and the original intuitionistic preorder is contained in that specialization preorder because every open was assumed upward closed. In the finite quotient poset, the union of maximal specialization classes is open and meets every principal open; conversely every dense open must contain each maximal class, so this union is the unique least dense open. On a chain, the available up-sets are nested tails, so any subfamily containing the empty set and whole set is a topology, giving exactly 2^(n-1) choices and the stated multiplicities by fixing the least selected nonempty tail.

originality.rationale: The final claim is a direct assembly of standard finite-topology facts with Sedlár's published dense-open characterization of coherent justification. The finite-space specialization theorem already identifies every finite topology with the Alexandrov topology of its specialization preorder. Once that theorem is invoked, the least dense open as the maximal specialization classes is an elementary finite-poset observation, and the chain census is the immediate count of subfamilies of a nested set of tails. Under implication-based originality, the absence of the exact combined sentence in the evidence-logic paper does not make these textbook consequences original.
